title: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network
key_facts: US President Donald Trump denied limiting Ukraine's access to Starshield, Starlink's military-grade sister network, after it restricted drone speed.
Trump said it was not him and he did not think it was Elon Musk, and that he was not sure Starshield ever came down.

Musk suggested the US government, possibly the Pentagon, managed Starshield and might have been behind the restrictions; Reuters reported on Thursday, citing two unnamed US officials and a Western official, that the order came from inside the White House.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the usual speed had not been restored.
On Tuesday night the network restricted speed to 100 mph (160 km/h), so weapons travelling faster lost connectivity; Ukraine was hit by several deadly strikes on Tuesday after the slowdown.
A bipartisan group of US senators signed a letter demanding an investigation into the disruption.
quote_evidence: US President Donald Trump has denied limiting Ukraine's access to Starlink's sister internet network Starshield after it restricted drone speed, hampering Kyiv's ability to protect itself from Russian attacks.
Musk himself suggested the US government might have been behind the restrictions, while news agency Reuters reported on Thursday that the order had come from inside the White House.
In its report about the alleged order regarding Starshield, Reuters quoted two unnamed US officials and a Western official briefed on the matter.
why_it_matters_hint: A speed limit on the military internet network cut off fast Ukrainian drones, and who ordered it is disputed between Trump, Musk and Reuters' sources.
event_date: 16 Oct 2026 (Trump's denial, Friday); the speed limit was on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026; Reuters report Thursday 15 Oct 2026
notes: REPLY STORY: Trump answers a Reuters report of Thursday 15 Oct and Musk's suggestion. The Reuters report was not carried in our recent editions. Zelensky's remark and the senators' letter are as the BBC states them. The BBC text mixes Starlink and Starshield; I follow its wording for the denial (Starshield).
